title: Your Credit Score Just Got Faster: RBI's New Weekly Reporting Rules
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has changed how your credit information is reported. Banks and lenders now send your loan and credit card data to credit burea.

faq.a: A credit bureau, like CIBIL, is a company that collects and maintains credit information about individuals from various lenders and then provides this information in the form of a credit report and score to other lenders when you apply for a loan or credit card.

faq.q: Does this apply to all my loans and credit cards?
faq.a: Yes, these new rules apply to all types of loans (home, personal, vehicle, etc.) and credit cards issued by banks and NBFCs regulated by the RBI.

faq.q: How can I check my updated credit score?
faq.a: You are entitled to one free full credit report from each credit bureau every year. You can access these directly from the websites of the credit bureaus (like TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, CRIF High Mark, Equifax) or through various financial platforms.

faq.q: What if I find an error in my credit report?
faq.a: If you find an error, you should immediately raise a dispute with the credit bureau. Under the new rules, they are mandated to resolve your dispute within 30 days.

faq.q: Will this make it harder to get a loan?
faq.a: Not necessarily. For disciplined borrowers, it can be beneficial as good repayment behaviour will be reflected faster. However, if you have a history of missed payments or high credit utilisation, those negative aspects will also appear sooner, potentially impacting new loan applications more quickly.
